headline: Majors hold above 200-day lines with momentum stalling, while whales move $227M onto exchanges over 72 hours and Bitcoin ETF outflows persist.
paragraphs: All seven majors sit above their 200-day simple moving averages, and five carry active golden crosses: BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP, and BNB are in confirmed uptrends by that measure. The regime is constructive. However, momentum tells a different story. Every major asset reports MACD below its signal line, meaning the 12/26-day momentum cross has turned bearish across the board. RSI-14 readings cluster in the 48 to 59 range, neutral to slightly overbought but nowhere near exhaustion. The contradiction is the day's frame: trend structure intact, momentum quietly diverging lower. This is not capitulation; it is rest, or the beginning of a test.

Funding rates on perpetual futures reveal patience being priced in. Bitcoin and Ethereum charge 0.0062% and 0.0067% per eight-hour interval, annualizing to 6.8% and 7.3% respectively. These are moderate, not hot. Solana is warmer at 0.0096% (10.5% annualized), and XRP and DOGE pull harder at 0.01% and 0.0057%, with annualized equivalents of 11% and 6.3%. Long-side crowding shows up in the ratios: Solana longs outnumber shorts 2.01 to 1, XRP sits at 2.39 to 1, and Doge reaches 4.24 to 1. Bitcoin and Ethereum are more balanced at 1.45 and 1.33. The imbalance in the alts signals a one-way bet in smaller venues; Bitcoin's moderate ratio and lower funding suggest the smart money has paid for its leverage and is sitting still. Liquidations over the past 1 to 16 hours (windows vary by asset) show shorts taking damage in Bitcoin (zero long liquidations, $484k in shorts) and Ethereum ($471k longs to $187k shorts), a pattern consistent with a rally attempting to hold. Solana and XRP flip this, with longs blowing up harder, a tension worth watching as price tests conviction.

Bitcoin is down 0.04% on the day and down 3.6% over seven days, yet up 20.9% over 30 days. Ethereum moves up 0.3% on the day and up 1.1% week-to-week, with a 31.9% monthly gain. Solana is up 0.3% on the day but down 2.2% on the week, gaining 35.5% in the month. These overlapping time windows reveal no unified signal: some assets are grinding in the session (BTC flat, ETH and SOL slightly green) while the week shows mixed resolution and the month confirms the bull leg. This layering is normal for a consolidation phase within a longer rally. The 90-day ranges tell the real story. Bitcoin sits at 76,790, well below its 12-month high of 124,740 (down 38.4%), Ethereum is 2,484 versus 4,691 (down 47%), and Solana trades at 99.66 versus 247.60 (down 59.7%). Doge and Ada are cut deepest: down 70.7% and 77.9% respectively from yearly peaks. These are not new assets in all-time high mode; they are assets returning from significant drawdowns.

Whale flows over the last 72 hours show $227 million moving onto exchanges, driven by Bitcoin at $167 million net inbound to exchange wallets (gross inflow of $470M, gross outflow of $243M). Larger stablecoin moves accompany this: $171 million USDC to Kraken, $157 million USDT to Binance, signaling dry powder arrival at venues. This intake contrasts with the weekly data, which shows a consistent pattern of coins moving onto exchanges: week ending Aug 24 saw $807 million arrive, Aug 31 brought $513 million, Sep 07 was quiet at $38 million, and this past week (Sep 14) reversed sharply with $725 million moving onto exchanges. The trend is accumulation and staging. Bitcoin ETF flows reinforce caution: the latest session (Sep 11) shows a $13.2 million outflow, and the five-session sum is negative $288.1 million with four days pointing the same direction. Ethereum ETF flows sing a different tune, with $216.4 million flowing in on Sep 11 and $222.8 million cumulative over five sessions, a unanimous pattern. This divergence, Bitcoin out and Ethereum in via traditional finance channels, suggests institutional players are rotating or that Ethereum's recent leverage and price action is attracting fresh TradFi demand.

Sentiment sits at 57 (Greed), comfortably above the 30-day floor of 31 but well below the ceiling of 74. The 30-day range is wide, signaling volatility in risk appetite. Stablecoin float stands at $310 billion, up 1.23% on the month, a modest expansion that does not scream urgency in either direction. Total market cap edged down 0.14% in the last 24 hours to $2.69 trillion. Bitcoin dominance holds at 58.5%, firm but not dominant enough to suggest a capitulation-driven escape. Bitcoin network difficulty is set to increase 4.3% at retarget (706 blocks to go), a small but meaningful tightening that reflects recent miner confidence in hash rate contributions.

Watch for two hinge points. First, whether all-major MACD crosses above signal within the next several candles, which would re-align momentum with the standing uptrend and remove the divergence. That would confirm the consolidation as orderly rather than a preliminary topping. Second, track the direction of Bitcoin ETF flows: the current four-session outflow could reverse, matching Ethereum's inbound pattern, or persist and suggest institutional skepticism widening. A return of Bitcoin to its 200-day line (currently around 68,000 by structure) would be a technical stress point; a reclaim of the 81,265 spark high would test whether the week's dip is done.
